name: Material
description: Physical material, vessel and lighting properties of a Liquid Watch liquid. The simulator derives every legacy Params field from these (sim/src/material/derive.ts); nothing here is sent to firmware directly. All values at 20 °C and 1 atm unless a preset's provenance says otherwise.

fields.label: Refractive index
fields.help: Refractive index of the liquid at 20 °C (water 1.333, olive oil 1.47, honey 1.49, ethanol 1.36). Sets the Fresnel reflections at the wall–liquid interface, the depth warp of marks behind the liquid and the wall specular seen over it.

fields.label: Absorption red
fields.help: Absorption coefficient K of the red channel (Beer–Lambert / Kubelka–Munk). 0 = colourless; 0.1/mm tints a 4.5 mm chord to 64 %; 1/mm makes it opaque-dark; whole blood ≈ (1, 20, 25)/mm.

fields.label: Absorption green
fields.help: Absorption coefficient K of the green channel.

fields.label: Absorption blue
fields.help: Absorption coefficient K of the blue channel.

fields.label: Scattering (reduced)
fields.help: Reduced scattering coefficient S = μs·(1−g) of the bulk (two-flux Kubelka–Munk). 0 = clear; milk ≈ 3/mm, blood ≈ 1/mm (with strong green/blue absorption), ink ≈ 0. Scattering makes the body opaque and Lambert-shaded instead of see-through.

fields.label: Emission red
fields.help: Self-emitted radiance of the liquid, red channel, relative to the diffuse illumination unit (1 = as bright as a white surface under the light). 0 for ordinary liquids; glow sticks, plasma and molten metal are the only emitters.

fields.label: Emission green
fields.help: Self-emitted radiance, green channel.

fields.label: Emission blue
fields.help: Self-emitted radiance, blue channel.

fields.label: Metallic
fields.help: 1 = a liquid metal (mercury, molten iron): opaque conductor, mirror specular, no transmission; the absorption and scattering fields are ignored. 0 = dielectric liquid.

fields.label: Metal reflectance
fields.help: Neutral (grey) reflectance of the metal surface; only used when metallic = 1 (mercury 0.75, molten iron 0.3 + emission).

fields.label: Phase
fields.help: 0 = liquid. 1 = plasma / gas discharge: no inertia, no slug, no meniscus dynamics, no film, no residue, no bubbles; must emit light. Xenon is the reference.

fields.label: Density
fields.help: Mass density at 20 °C (water 1000, ethanol 789, olive oil 915, honey 1420, mercury 13546, molten iron 7000; a gas/plasma column such as xenon 5.9). Enters the capillary length, the Bond number, the viscous drag coordinate and the bubble rise speed.

fields.label: Dynamic viscosity
fields.help: Dynamic viscosity μ at 20 °C (liquid oxygen 0.19, water 1.0, champagne 1.5, blood 4, olive oil 84, honey 10000). Drives slug drag, end bounce, surface damping, the dynamic contact angle, the trailing film, residue drain-back and bubble rise — all through one number.

fields.label: Surface tension
fields.help: Liquid–air surface tension γ at 20 °C (water 72, ethanol 22, olive oil 32, honey ≈ 70, mercury 485, molten iron ≈ 1800). Sets the capillary length √(γ/ρg), the meniscus spring and the capillary number.

fields.label: Contact angle
fields.help: Static contact angle of the liquid on the vessel wall (water on clean glass 20°, oil on acrylic 15°, mercury on glass 140°). Below 90° the meniscus is concave (wetting), above it a convex bead. The band angle ± hysteresis must not cross 90°.

fields.label: Contact-angle hysteresis
fields.help: Half-band of the advancing/receding angles around the static angle: a contact line advances at θ + h and recedes at θ − h (clean glass 5–10°, rough or coated walls 15–25°). Larger hysteresis pins the liquid longer before it moves.

fields.label: Non-volatile solids
fields.help: Fraction of the liquid left on the wall as a stain when its film dries (water 0, wine 0.02, blood 0.45, ink 0.5, honey 0.8). 0 = a receding edge leaves no residue. Only wetting liquids leave residue.

fields.label: Drying time
fields.help: Time constant for the wall film to dry into its stain, on the watch's compressed time scale (1 s ≈ a minute of real drying). Tilting drains the film faster.

fields.label: Gas
fields.help: 0 none; 1 dissolved gas (carbonation: a steady rising bead, watery liquids only); 2 boiling (dense fast bubbles, cryogenic liquids); 3 trapped air (slow bubbles held in a medium or viscous liquid: a few to a dense suspension).

fields.label: Gas level
fields.help: How much gas: nucleation density of the bead (bubble count) within the mode's range.

fields.label: Bubble radius
fields.help: Typical bubble radius (champagne 0.05, beer 0.1, trapped air in honey 0.12). Sets the drawn size and, with viscosity and density, the Stokes rise speed.

fields.label: Foam stability
fields.help: Mean time a bubble survives at the surface before it pops (pure water < 1 s, beer/champagne 3–5 s, viscous or surfactant-rich liquids 10–30 s). 0 = bubbles vanish at the surface.

fields.label: Inner radius
fields.help: Bore radius of the vessel. Sets every chord length (optical depth), the Bond number, the drag coordinate μ/(ρr²) and the bubble/film scales. The drawn tube height is a separate layout choice (the panel shows the tube through a magnifying rod).

fields.label: Wall thickness
fields.help: Glass/acrylic wall thickness: the dark silhouette band of the tube where rays pass through wall only.

fields.label: Wall refractive index
fields.help: Refractive index of the vessel wall (acrylic 1.49, borosilicate 1.47, soda-lime 1.52). With the liquid index it sets the interface reflections and the wall specular over the liquid.

fields.label: Light elevation
fields.help: Angle of the room light above the panel normal in the tube's cross-section. The specular highlight sits at half this angle from the centre row. Used directly for self-lit liquids; ordinary liquids take the world-up light from the IMU.

fields.label: Light size
fields.help: Angular size (FWHM) of the light source: a small lamp 10°, a window 40–60°. Sets the highlight band width and softness.

fields.label: Light intensity
fields.help: Radiance of the light relative to a normal room lamp (1). Sets the specular highlights on liquid and glass and the diffuse illumination of the backing.

fields.label: Ambient light
fields.help: Diffuse environment fill relative to the light: lifts the shaded side of the body and the empty wall, and desaturates bright reflections toward white.

fields.label: Exposure
fields.help: Display exposure of the whole scene (art direction, not a material property): scales the illumination before encoding to the panel.

design.description: Legacy Params keys a physical preset may set directly: watch design, layout, marks and behaviour. Every other Params key is derived or fixed by derive.ts (table in docs/physical-renderer.md). derive() rejects a design that contradicts the material (rear marks behind an opaque liquid, a bright backing behind an emissive one, a free slug for plasma).
